unit.title: How deep to plant a seed
unit.needIt: Most seeds that never come up were buried too deep. One simple rule about covering them fixes that.
unit.why: A gardener wants to grow a big crop but covers the tiny seeds too deep. The seeds stay hidden and never wake up. By learning the right depth, the gardener ensures every seed has a chance to reach the sun.
unit.outcome: Plant seeds at the correct depth to ensure they sprout.
unit.reachesYou: You see seeds in the grocery store aisle or on a garden website. You might see your neighbors working in their backyard plots.
unit.do: Find a small seed and place it on the soil surface. Press it down gently with your hand to see how it sits.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake people make when planting seeds?
quiz.why: The text states that people often cover seeds too deeply.
quiz.quote: OST persons make the serious mistake of covering garden seed too deeply.

quiz.q: How should very small seeds be planted?
quiz.why: Small seeds do best when scattered on the surface and pressed down.
quiz.quote: Very small seed needs hardly any covering. Indeed, it does its best, as a general thing, when simply scattered on the surface and pressed down into the soil by a smooth board.

quiz.q: What should you do if you do not have a seed-sower?
quiz.why: The text says to draw a stick through the soil to make furrows.
quiz.quote: If a seed-sower is not used, little furrows should be made by drawing a stick through the soil, into which the seed should be dropped as evenly as possible.

quiz.q: What should you do with extra seedlings that grow?
quiz.why: Surplus seedlings should be removed once they get a good start.
quiz.quote: These surplus seedlings should be removed from the rows as soon as the plants get a good start.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of using a seed-sower?
quiz.why: The seed-sower is described as a labor-saver in large gardens.
quiz.quote: but in large gardens it will be found as much a labor-saver as the garden-cultivator.

quiz.q: How can you have fresh vegetables throughout almost the entire season?
choices: By planting all seeds at once
By planting at intervals of ten days or two weeks
By using a seed-sower every day
quiz.why: The text explains that planting at intervals allows for a continuous supply of food.
quiz.quote: By planting at intervals of ten days or two weeks it is possible to have fresh vegetables throughout almost the entire season.

quiz.q: Why might a small garden choose later varieties?
quiz.why: Later varieties are often superior in flavor to earlier ones.
quiz.quote: In the small garden I would advise the choice of the later varieties, as these are almost without exception superior in flavor to the earlier kinds

partials: Small seeds need hardly any covering.

crystal.key: Proper planting depth and variety choice ensure a successful and tasty garden.

decoys.text: Deep soil is always better for all seeds.
decoys.why: The text says very small seeds fail if covered too deeply.

decoys.text: Early varieties are always the best choice.
decoys.why: The text says later varieties are usually superior in flavor.

crystal.aha: By matching the seed size to the correct depth and choosing the right variety, you get a better harvest.
